title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: the numbered notes of 'La Longue Marche' (page 39 of Grothendieck's own numbering). The previous page treats a degenerating situation. Over a strictly local base with generic point eta, a curve U = X \ T has a section f meeting a cusp g_{i0}(S) with intersection multiplicity mu, the length of the local Artinian intersection scheme. Grothendieck conjectures that the specialization map pi_1(eta) -> pi_1(U) ≅ pi_1(U_s) on prime-to-p fundamental groups is k_{i0} ∘ (mu·id_T). This page completes that statement. k_{i0} : T = T_∞(k) = lim mu_n(k) ≅ Ẑ'(1) -> pi_1(U_k) is the 'local' homomorphism attached to the cusp i0: the inclusion of the inertia group at the puncture, the fundamental group of a punctured formal disc. He admits this as 'hardly difficult'.

He then opens a new topic to end the section. Let X -> S be smooth and proper, a relative curve, and T ⊂ X finite étale over S (the cusp divisor), with U = X \ T. Suppose T has a given section s_{i0} over S, i.e. a cusp defined over S. Consider the homotopy extension 1 -> pi -> E_U -> E_S -> 1. Here pi = pi_1 of the geometric fibre (suitably completed, e.g. prime to the residue characteristics), E_U = pi_1(U) and E_S = pi_1(S). The cusp i0 defines a pi-conjugacy class of subgroups L_{i0} ⊂ pi: the inertia subgroups at that cusp, each ≅ T = Ẑ(1). He calls the associated objects the 'sections of the second kind' (cuspidal, as opposed to sections coming from S-points of U).

Left exactness of the sequence requires pi_2(S) -> pi_1(fibre) to vanish. He notes this holds if pi_2(S) = 0, e.g. when S is an Artin elementary neighbourhood ('modèle élémentaire') over a field of characteristic 0. He expects the characteristic-0 restriction to be unnecessary for prime-to-p groups.

The next page continues: the normalizer N(L_i) in E_U surjects onto E_S, giving an extension 1 -> T -> N(L_i) -> E_S -> 1 with class c_i ∈ H^2(E_S, T) ≅ H^2(S, Ẑ(1)) when S is K(pi,1). This class is to be compared via Kummer theory with Pic(S)^ ⊂ H^2(S, Ẑ(1)). The evident target, implicit here, is that c_i is the Chern class of the normal (or conormal) line bundle of the cusp section s_{i0}(S) in X. The tubular-neighbourhood intuition: the punctured normal bundle is a G_m-torsor whose pi_1-extension is classified by c_1(N). Consequently cuspidal ('tangential') splittings exist over E_S iff that class dies.
errors: Notational clash: T denotes both the finite étale cusp divisor in X and T = T_∞ = lim mu_n ≅ Ẑ(1).

The hypothesis pi_2(S)=0 is stronger than needed. For hyperbolic fibres, the image of pi_2(S) in pi_1(fibre) is central, and the (pro-l / prime-to-p completed) fibre group is centre-free. So the homotopy sequence is left exact automatically, in line with SGA1 XIII-type results. Grothendieck's marginal 'il faudrait vérifier ça!' signals the point is not settled for him.

The step 'normalizer of L_i maps onto E_S with kernel T' needs L_i to be self-normalizing in pi (true for hyperbolic fibres) and the Frattini-type argument (all conjugates of L_i in E_U are pi-conjugate). This is only asserted on the next page; with these it is correct.
The identification of the specialization map with k_{i0}∘(mu·id) is explicitly admitted without proof (and the case nu=1 was left aside on the previous page).

ideas.what: Inertia homomorphism at a cusp k_{i0}: Ẑ(1) -> pi_1(U_k) and its composition with multiplication by an intersection multiplicity to describe specialization of a section meeting a cusp
ideas.modern_name: cuspidal inertia subgroup; local monodromy / tame specialization

ideas.what: Homotopy exact sequence 1->pi_1(fibre)->pi_1(U)->pi_1(S)->1 for a relative curve with good compactification, with left exactness when pi_2(S)=0 (S an Artin elementary neighbourhood, K(pi,1))
ideas.modern_name: homotopy exact sequence for families of hyperbolic curves; Artin good neighbourhoods are K(pi,1)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck SGA1 XIII; M. Artin SGA4 XI

ideas.what: Cuspidal decomposition groups over the base: conjugacy class L_{i0} attached to a cusp section, its normalizer giving an extension of pi_1(S) by Ẑ(1), and 'sections of the second kind'
ideas.modern_name: cuspidal decomposition groups / cuspidal (tangential) sections in anabelian geometry
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (tangential base points, 1989), Nakamura, Mochizuki, Hoshi (cuspidal sections)
ideas.where_published: Possibly alluded to in the 1983 letter to Faltings (sections at infinity); not developed in published texts

ideas.what: Extension class c_i ∈ H^2(pi_1(S), Ẑ(1)) compared to Pic(S)^ via Kummer, implicitly the Chern class of the normal bundle of the cusp section
ideas.modern_name: Euler/Chern class of the punctured normal bundle; obstruction to tangential base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore in topology (circle-bundle Euler class); in anabelian context Nakamura, Hoshi–Mochizuki

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a programme to compute the class c_i of the normalizer extension of a cuspidal inertia group over pi_1(S) via Kummer theory and Pic(S), i.e. a relative/family version of cuspidal sections. This anticipates later work on tangential base points and cuspidal sections in families, but the computation is not carried out on this page.
missed.quote: les "sections de 2ème espèce" de l'extension 1 → π → E_U → E_S → 1 associées à i_0 — qui définit une classe de π-conj. de sous-groupes L_{i_0} de π
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Shows Grothendieck treating cuspidal ('second kind') sections and their obstruction class (normal bundle Chern class) in a relative setting circa 1981, before Deligne's tangential base points. This is of historical interest for the section conjecture, but the mathematics is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The setup is standard (inertia at cusps, homotopy sequence, normalizer extension), though the terminology 'sections de 2ème espèce' and the early relative treatment of cuspidal decomposition classes are a mild historical point; nothing is finished here.
transcription_corrections: 'les "sections de gi[?] associées[?]"' should read approximately 'les "sections de 2ième espèce" de l'extension'.
'une section de T sur S' appears to read 'une section s_{i_0} donnée de T sur S'.
'qui définit une {+classe de π-conj. de+} (H-?)[?] sous-groupes[?]' should read 'qui définit une classe de π-conj. de sous-groupes L_{i_0} de π'.

'(je présume)' likely belongs with 'p.ex.' and the clause continues 'si on est dans le cas d'un modèle élémentaire au-dessus d'un corps de car. zéro (la restriction de car. nulle étant sans doute inutile, si on se borne aux groupes fondamentaux premiers aux car. résiduelles)'.
